Identity.Name: AppleTree
Identity.Description: An apple in blossom: a short trunk under a domed crown, wider than it is tall, with pink blossom dabbed through it - the cottage garden's apple.

Identity.Name: AshTree
Identity.Description: A tall ash: a long clear trunk and an open crown of masses, branches drawn partly through it - the tree behind the cottage.

Identity.Name: MatureOak
Identity.Description: A mature English oak: a short, leaning trunk under a broad, lumpy crown, its outline broken toward the light and its branches seen through the canopy.

Identity.Name: FieldMaple
Identity.Description: A field maple: a medium tree with a rounded crown on a short trunk - the garden's corner tree.

Identity.Name: SilverBirch
Identity.Description: A silver birch: a slender trunk and a small, light crown - the birch by the pond.

Identity.Name: EnglishYew
Identity.Description: An English yew: a short trunk and a dark stack of masses narrowing to the top, drawn with needle ticks.

Identity.Name: GardenShrub
Identity.Description: A large garden shrub: a domed mound of foliage masses with a scalloped outline and cupped shade beneath.

Identity.Name: GardenShrub
Identity.Description: A medium garden shrub: the same habit as the large one, a size smaller.

Identity.Name: GardenShrub
Identity.Description: A low flowering shrub, flecked with cream flowers - the one by the front fence.

Identity.Name: Hydrangea
Identity.Description: A mophead hydrangea: a rounded shrub carrying big heads of soft blue flowers.

Identity.Name: ShrubRose
Identity.Description: A shrub rose: an upright bush of arcing foliage dotted with pink roses - either side of the cottage door.

Identity.Name: ClippedHedge
Identity.Description: A clipped garden hedge, 3.6 m of it: a run of masses with a firm, scalloped top, its face turned to the view when placed.

Identity.Name: BoxBall
Identity.Description: A clipped box ball, dark and dense - one each side of the garden gate.

Identity.Name: BoxCone
Identity.Description: A clipped box cone: broad at the foot and pointed at the top, drawn with the clipped hedge's firm outline.

Identity.Name: PottedStandard
Identity.Description: A clipped ball on a clear stem in a square lead planter, a panel on each face and a tuft of strap leaves over the lip - the pair either side of an orangery's doors.

Identity.Name: PottedStandard
Identity.Description: The smaller potted standard: a tighter ball on a shorter stem in a smaller lead planter, for a doorstep or a narrow pier.

Identity.Name: Lavender
Identity.Description: A lavender clump: grey-green spikes under purple flower heads - the front border's.

Identity.Name: Lavender
Identity.Description: A low lavender for path edging: the same plant, smaller and tighter.

Identity.Name: Hollyhock
Identity.Description: A hollyhock: a tall leaning spire of leaves and mixed flowers on one stem - against the cottage wall.

Identity.Name: Foxglove
Identity.Description: A foxglove: a spire of pink bells on a single stem - in the fence border.

Identity.Name: Catmint
Identity.Description: Catmint: a soft grey-green mound hazed with small blue flowers.

Identity.Name: Chamomile
Identity.Description: Chamomile: a feathery deep green mound starred with white daisies.

Identity.Name: Calendula
Identity.Description: Calendula: a bright mound of pot marigolds, orange flowers over light green.

Identity.Name: OrnamentalGrass
Identity.Description: An ornamental grass: a low crown and tapering blades arching out and leaning with the wind.

Identity.Name: Reeds
Identity.Description: Reeds at a margin: a narrow crown and upright blades - at the pond's edge.

Identity.Name: PicketFencePanel
Identity.Description: A 2.4 m panel of white picket fence: posts and caps, two rails behind, pointed pickets in front - the front fence's.

Identity.Name: GardenBench
Identity.Description: A weathered timber garden bench: seat, back and four legs, turned to face the view when placed - the bench by the pond.

Identity.Name: TerracottaPlanter
Identity.Description: A flared terracotta planter of ornamental grass - the pair either side of the cottage step.
